approach: Use the authors' GitHub repository as the source of truth. First check whether Rscript exists; if it does, reproduce.py invokes the authors' code_11_table3.R as-is and parses the Lymphoma MNAR0 30% row. Because the sandbox is Python-only, the executable fallback is a faithful Python transliteration of code_01_functions.R and only the C1 block of code_11_table3.R: it loads Lymphoma, reproduces the exact MNAR0 30% mask generator, selects lambda by the repository's instability criterion, fits MNAR-k-means and k-POD (lambda=0), computes pairwise CER over 10 repetitions, and writes results/metrics.json. The port changes language only, not the method, and is validated by checking that k-POD lands near the paper's 0.279 before trusting the proposed 0.029.

files.purpose: Pin Python packages used by the fallback: numpy, scipy, pandas, scikit-learn.
Load lymphoma.x/y, reproduce the author MNAR0 mask from code_11_table3.R, and compute pairwise CER and optional MSE.
Core MNAR-k-means: mean-imputation + k-means++ initialization, binary membership update, penalized center update, loss, and full fit; k-POD is the lambda=0 path.
Port the repository instability criterion for selecting lambda from {2,4,6,8,10}; fall back to A8 only if the author code lacks an explicit implementation.
Run C1: 10 repetitions of Lymphoma k=3 MNAR0 30%, proposed vs k-POD, collecting per-repetition CERs and selected lambdas.
Single entrypoint. Prefer Rscript code_11_table3.R if R is available; otherwise call run_c1.py. Write results/metrics.json.

config.missing_mechanism: MNAR0, 30% (C1; copy exact generator from code_11_table3.R)
config.n_init_instability: 20 (runtime assumption for lambda selection; final fits use 100)
config.tol: relative loss change < 1e-6 or U unchanged (A3)
config.mse_metric: sum_l min_l' ||mu_l - mu_l'||^2 (R8; report only if true centers are available)

steps: Clone https://github.com/GXguanxin/MNAR-k-means into repo/ with git if it is not already present.

Inspect code_11_table3.R, code_01_functions.R, and initcenters_oncepkpod_functions.cpp; record the exact C1 block: Lymphoma loading, MNAR0 30% mask generation, lambda grid, instability selection, CER, and random seeds.
Check for R with python -c "import shutil; print(shutil.which('Rscript'))".

If Rscript exists: run the authors' code_11_table3.R as-is (or the smallest existing invocation that produces Table 3), capture the MNAR0 30% proposed and k-POD CER values, and write them to results/metrics.json. Do not alter the method.
If Rscript is absent: create requirements.txt and pip-install any missing Python packages from it.
Implement data_utils.py by direct transliteration of the author data loader and MNAR0 mask code; verify X is 62x4026, y has 62 labels, and the three class counts match the Lymphoma labels.
Implement mnar_kmeans.py with k-means++ initialization on column-mean-imputed data, membership update Eq.(7)/(8), center update Algorithm 1 line 4, empty-cluster retention, and lambda=0 as k-POD.
Implement instability.py to match the repository criterion; if the repository does not expose it clearly, use A8 (10 repeats, m=floor(n/3)).

Implement run_c1.py: for each of 10 repetitions, generate the MNAR0 30% mask, select lambda on {2,4,6,8,10}, fit proposed with 100 initializations, fit k-POD with 100 initializations, compute pairwise CER against the true labels, and store per-repetition results.

Implement reproduce.py to prefer the R path and otherwise call run_c1.py; always write results/metrics.json with claim_id C1, proposed CER, k-POD CER, SD, per-repetition CERs, selected lambdas, config, and elapsed time.
Run the smoke test, then the full C1 run, then validate the result against the paper's 0.029 +/- 0.03 tolerance and the k-POD sanity value near 0.279.
smoke_test: python reproduce.py --smoke: load Lymphoma, use 2 repetitions, lambda grid {2,10}, 5 initializations, max_iter=20, and write results/smoke_metrics.json. Assert CERs are finite, the k-POD CER is above 0.20, and the proposed CER is no worse than k-POD on the smoke run.
intermediate_checks: Confirm lymphoma.x.txt loads as X with shape (62, 4026) after any necessary transpose, and lymphoma.y.txt has length 62 with exactly 3 classes.
Confirm the reproduced MNAR0 30% mask has missing rate approximately 0.30 and that no row is entirely missing; if any all-missing rows occur, drop them per R12.
Confirm the pairwise CER implementation gives 0 when two labelings are identical up to permutation and approximately 0.5-0.7 for random balanced labelings on n=62.
Confirm k-POD (lambda=0) on Lymphoma MNAR0 30% gives CER in the paper's neighborhood, about 0.279 +/- 0.03; this is the strongest check that the mask and clustering port are faithful.
Confirm the proposed method with lambda=0 is exactly the k-POD path.
Confirm the objective decreases monotonically within each fit and that selected lambdas are not all at a grid boundary.
Confirm final fits use 100 initializations and max 100 iterations; if runtime forces a scale-down, record the reduced values in metrics.json and use at least 5 repetitions.
budget_plan: 0-5 min: clone repo, inspect the two R files and C++ helper, check Rscript. 5-10 min: if R exists, set up/run author Table 3; otherwise implement the Python transliteration. 10-12 min: smoke test and the k-POD sanity check. 12-24 min: full C1 run with 10 repetitions and 100 initializations per final fit. 24-25 min: write results/metrics.json and validate the reported CER against C1. If the full run exceeds budget, reduce to 5 repetitions and 20 initializations for lambda selection only, keeping 100 initializations for final proposed/k-POD fits.
